To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of intronic riboprobes, which measure hnRNA levels, provides a new and important approach to the study of gene expression in the CNS.

(1) intronic riboprobes can be used for in situ hybridization to measure the levels of hnRNA in neurons, and (2) the combination of exon- and intronic probes can be used to study the relative contributions of transcription and mRNA decay in changes of gene expression in response to physiological stimuli.

the use of intronic probes to measure gene expression by ISHH can be a valuable tool for the study of the regulation of gene expression in the central nervous system, and that intronic probes can be used to study the regulation of gene transcription and mRNA stability.

elucidating the mechanisms underlying the regulation of gene expression in the neuroendocrine system.
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of OT and VP gene transcription.
the development of new molecular tools for studying gene expression in the brain, and with the application of these tools to the study of gene expression in the magnocellular hypothalamic neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute osmotic stimulation results in increased VP gene expression, but not OT gene expression.
the OT and VP genes are regulated differently in magnocellular neurons, and that the use of intronic probes is a powerful new tool for studying gene expression.

the changes observed in the levels of OT and VP mRNA and hnRNA in the hypothalamic magnocellular neurons are the result of a complex interaction between changes in gene transcription and mRNA degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acute hyperosmolality increases both OT and VP gene transcription, whereas lactation increases OT gene transcription and decreases VP mRNA degradation.

the changes in OT and VP gene transcription in response to lactation and acute salt loading, respectively, are not large enough to account for the large changes in the steady-state levels of these two neuropeptides.
lactation increases OT gene expression by decreasing OT mRNA degradation, whereas acute hyperosmolar stimuli increase VP gene expression by increasing VP transcription.
